answer: To block sybils an agent economy can require each identity to climb a sequential summit of verification: the agent first obtains a unique inlet token from a random peer quorum, then threads a continuous low-bandwidth proof stream that must be re-validated at every height. An attacker running many hollow identities cannot share the inlet or the thread because each is bound to a single key and the summit check is peer-local; the cost is ongoing bandwidth and latency per identity that scales linearly and cannot be amortized.
